content: Fluticasone is a corticosteroid medication that is prescribed to reduce inflammation and alleviate symptoms such as itching, redness, dryness, and scaling that are associated with various skin conditions. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Fluticasone is available in the form of an ointment or cream that is applied directly to the skin. Typically, it is used two to four times daily at evenly spaced intervals. It is essential to follow the instructions provided on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or need clarification, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Use the medication exactly as directed, without applying more or less than prescribed or using it more frequently than instructed. Do not discontinue the medication without first consulting your doctor. Before application, clean the affected area thoroughly, allow it to dry, and then gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it is absorbed. Use only enough to cover the affected area. After applying the medication, wash your hands thoroughly. If you are using the scalp lotion, apply it directly to the affected area using the squeeze bottle. Before starting fluticasone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to fluticasone or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently using, especially skin products containing hydrocortisone or vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have any other medical conditions, infections, or allergies. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using fluticasone, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Fluticasone may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: itching, burning, swelling, redness, skin rash, or numbness in the fingers. Store fluticasone in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. Fluticasone is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless specifically instructed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Fluticasone is sold under the brand name Cutivate®.
